clue.text: Returning fairy queen gets aggressive in carriage

indicators.note: in tells us the aggressive word sits inside the turned-round queen's name
returning sends the fairy queen's name back the way it came, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, named in Romeo and Juliet
aggressive play can be called rough

explanation.surface: A fairy queen on her way home turns violent inside her coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Mab is the fairy queen in Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet. 'Returning' makes BAM, which 'in' wraps around the word for aggressive; the definition is the last word, a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn closed vehicle, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Eritrea being transformed, needing time and energy to be state again?

indicators.note: being transformed says the country's letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Is Eritrea, remade with time and energy, going to become a state once more?
explanation.walkthrough: 'being transformed' gives REITERA. 'State' looks like a nation, matching the country in the surface, but here it is the verb meaning say, and 'again' completes the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to repeat something said, saying it over once more.

clue.text: Absolutely say

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is loose: the adjective means absolute or complete, as in 'utter nonsense', so the clue's adverb stands for that whole-hearted sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or total; as a verb it means to speak or voice words.

clue.text: One needs a bit of brain in a place where beastly types study?

parts.words: One needs a bit of brain in a place where beastly types study?
parts.note: a university grounds for river horses would be where such beasts study, and everyone has this brain part

explanation.surface: Anyone needs brains to get into a college where animals learn.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it in two: HIPPO, a beastly type, plus CAMPUS, a place to study, gives the name of the brain structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippocampus is the seahorse-shaped region in each temporal lobe that handles memory.

clue.text: The possible source of a religious calling

definitions.text: The possible source of a religious calling

parts.words: The possible source of a religious calling
parts.note: the reading is of a vocation to the priesthood, but the calling is the muezzin's call to prayer from a mosque tower

explanation.surface: Where might someone's vocation to the church come from?
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the tall mosque tower from which the muezzin calls the faithful to prayer.

clue.text: Expression of impatience by former female tennis star getting dejected

parts.note: Maureen Connolly, the 1950s American champion, was known as Little Mo
pish is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience

explanation.surface: A retired women's tennis champion snorts impatiently and gets downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Mo was the nickname of Maureen Connolly, who won all four tennis majors in 1953; crossword setters use it as a stock source of the letters MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopish means given to moping, gloomy and low in spirits.

clue.text: Quiet member of the family

explanation.definitionFit: Mum means silent, as in keeping quiet; it is also an informal word for mother.

clue.text: Gym beginning to revitalise one-time player

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: beginning to asks for only the opening letter of revitalise

parts.note: one-time means former, as in a one-time champion

explanation.surface: A former sportsman starts going to the gym to get back into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is an actor or musician, someone who plays.

clue.text: Material wobbled, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for wobbled is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: something that wobbled swayed from side to side

explanation.surface: Some fabric shook, so people report.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, used as a fabric for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Able to squash a command

indicators.note: to squash means the word for able is pressed around the letter A, holding it inside

parts.note: able to do something means fit to do it

explanation.surface: Being capable of crushing an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or order.

clue.text: Animal to lose strength going to market, with death shortly following

parts.note: to pine is to waste away and lose strength
mart is a short word for a market

indicators.note: shortly means the word for death is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: end can mean death, as in come to a sticky end

explanation.surface: A creature weakens on its way to market, where it soon dies.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a weasel-like mammal of forests in Britain and Europe.

clue.text: The odd fish gets to finish on the far side of the dam

indicators.note: on the far side of means the finishing word comes after the dam, beyond it

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
to do can mean to finish, as in 'have you done?'

explanation.surface: A strange fish reaches the end of its journey beyond the weir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odd fish' looks like a creature in the river, but it is a person: 'odd fish' is slang for an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is an eccentric person, a strange character, which is what a weirdo is.

clue.text: Each boy should be in a particular colour, it's argued

indicators.note: be in tells us the first two pieces sit inside the colour word

parts.note: red is one particular colour
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone argues every lad ought to be dressed in a certain colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be in' is the container signal. The definition 'it's argued' must be read as 'it is reasoned', the past participle, not as a statement about a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoned means argued logically, as in a reasoned case.

clue.text: Line up chaps in cunning configuration

indicators.note: in tells us the lining-up word and the chaps sit inside the word for cunning

parts.note: art can mean cunning or trickery, as in artful
to range things is to set them out in a row
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Set some fellows in a row in a clever pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement is a layout or setup of parts, the same idea as a configuration.

clue.text: One trying to control players brands team "lousy"

indicators.note: lousy means bad or poor, so the two words are badly arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach calls his own side rubbish, labelling them so.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandmaster conducts a band, directing its musicians.

clue.text: Ultimately light-hearted relationship?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word light-hearted

parts.note: an alliance is a relationship or union

explanation.surface: In the end, is it just a casual affair?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the last letter of 'light-hearted' plus ALLIANCE, and also a fair description of a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or sexual affair, a frivolous liaison.

clue.text: Plans the return of unwanted mail?

indicators.note: the return of means the word for junk mail is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

explanation.surface: Schemes for sending back junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are plans or charts, as in a street plan.

clue.text: I pursue no fancy, being hard up

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are worked into a decorative new order

explanation.surface: Someone too poor to follow any whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Penurious means extremely poor, short of money.

clue.text: In good health in spring

explanation.definitionFit: Well means healthy; a well is also a spring, a source of water from the ground.

clue.text: Pregnant, I start to regret casual coupling

indicators.note: casual means loose and unplanned, so the letters are thrown into a new order
start to asks for the opening letter of regret

explanation.surface: An expectant mother admits that she is beginning to regret a one-night stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual' rearranges PREGNANT, I and R (the first letter of 'regret', signalled by 'start to').
explanation.definitionFit: Partnering is the joining of two people as a pair, which is a coupling.

clue.text: Supposed place over which wild animals would head north

indicators.note: over which means in this down clue the animals sit over and around the placing word
head north means the animals word goes upwards in this down light, so it reads backwards

parts.note: deer are wild animals
to put is to place

explanation.surface: An assumed spot over which wild beasts would make their way north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'head north' means read upwards, so the animals become REED; 'over which' then sets them around the word for place. 'Supposed' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed to be, as in the reputed father.

clue.text: Pulls apart disorderly pupils crossing street, heading back

indicators.note: crossing means the jumbled schoolchildren straddle the street word, which sits within them
disorderly says the pupils are rearranged into a new order
heading back means the street abbreviation turns round, read right to left

explanation.surface: Unruly schoolchildren crossing a road are separated, then head back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' makes SPLIUP; 'heading back' gives TS, which 'crossing' places inside. 'Pulls apart' reads as a verb about a fight, matching the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate, as in pulling apart.

clue.text: Border gone over by very soft brush?

indicators.note: gone over by means the very soft letters cover the border word, one either side

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An edging trimmed using a delicate brush.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the musical direction pianissimo. The query on 'brush' flags that the definition is a loose one: brushing hair is one way to primp.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, such as by brushing one's hair.

clue.text: Bear with aim to get to northern river

parts.note: an end is an aim, as in ends and means
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Put up with the goal of reaching a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear, tolerate or put up with something.

clue.text: Medic's bad practice

parts.note: Dr is the title of a doctor, a medic
ill can mean bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A doctor's poor professional conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' looks like a medical practice, but it is the noun for repeated exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Drill is routine training by repetition, as in fire drill.

clue.text: Plant that could be processed to make e.g. Ointment

indicators.note: could be processed to make means the letters are worked through and turned into a new word

explanation.surface: A herb that could be prepared to make something like ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden herb with small greenish flowers.

clue.text: Academic turning up to give sign of approval

indicators.note: turning up means in this down clue the academic word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, an academic

explanation.surface: A lecturer who arrives to show he agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to dip the head as a gesture of agreement.

clue.text: A confession of action left one being seen as a hero

definitions.text: one being seen as a hero

parts.note: saying 'I do' declares that one performs the act

explanation.surface: Admitting to doing something left someone looking heroic.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person greatly admired or worshipped, a hero.

clue.text: Meal that leads to expansion?

explanation.surface: A big dinner that makes your waistline grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses join in a joke: a lavish meal leads to middle-age girth.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish meal laid out on a table; spread also means growth or widening.

clue.text: Daughter went on a diet, lacking a boyfriend to go out with?

definitions.text: lacking a boyfriend to go out with?

parts.note: someone on a diet ate less

explanation.surface: A girl is slimming because she has no boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Dateless describes someone without a romantic partner or evening appointment.
